title: Location tracking and maps that work offline
when: The phone app records positions or shows places on a map in areas with poor signal, so it must keep working and drawing without the network.
prompt:
Goal: Positions are recorded to the device with accuracy, and a map view draws points and tracks even with no network.
Steps:
1. After a tap: id = navigator.geolocation.watchPosition(save, onErr, { enableHighAccuracy: true, maximumAge: 5000 }); stop with clearWatch(id).
2. save() drops fixes with coords.accuracy over 50 m and points closer than 5 m to the last one, then writes { lat, lon, acc, t } to IndexedDB.
3. Draw the track on a <canvas> or SVG with a simple equirectangular projection around the track center; this needs no tiles at all.
4. For a base map ship your own small tile pack for the known area; bulk downloads from public tile servers break their usage policies.
5. Cache viewed tiles in a service worker cache with a size cap so revisited areas work offline.
6. Show the last known position with its age and an accuracy circle when a new fix is missing.
7. Compute distance with the haversine formula in a pure function that node:test can check.
8. Web pages cannot track with the screen off; continuous tracking needs a native background location plugin and a store justification.
Quality bar:
- Tracking stops when the user leaves the screen or taps stop.
- Offline the map still shows saved tracks.
Pitfalls:
- High accuracy forever, which drains the battery.
- Plotting raw jittery fixes.
Verify:
- [ ] clearWatch is called on stop.
- [ ] Inaccurate fixes are filtered.
- [ ] The map renders in airplane mode.
Output: track.js, mapview.js, geo.js with a test and the tile cache rule in sw.js.

examples.input: app de trilha que grava o percurso mesmo sem internet
examples.output: watchPosition with accuracy filter to IndexedDB, canvas track view, capped tile cache, haversine test
